key_insight: Higher child poverty is associated with less access to advanced mathematics, while stronger mathematics preparation is associated with better first-year grades across nearly every subject.
engineering_relevance: For engineering education, mathematics preparation and course design are potential targets for supporting first-year success, though intervention effects remain untested.
method: Link university entrants to sending schools and districts.
Compare course enrollment patterns with district child poverty.
Analyze preparation, grades, return rates, major changes, and mathematics section sizes.
evidence_signal: Fall 2014–Fall 2019 records from one broad-access Hispanic-Serving university show that mathematics was the largest single source of unsuccessful course outcomes among entrants who did not return after year one.
watch_item: Findings are associative, not causal; smaller mathematics sections require designed evaluation, and replication requires validated local data linkages.
paper_title: A Calculus Gradient: Child Poverty, Mathematics Preparation, and First-Year College Performance at a Hispanic-Serving University
